decision: The accordion keeps its closed blurbs findable
why: a reader searching the page for a phrase inside a closed item found nothing, and the prop that fixes that was documented and passed nowhere
evidence: driven: all three closed panels carry hidden until-found and keep their text, and dispatching beforematch on one drops the attribute, sets data-open and flips its trigger to expanded — Base UI listens for that event in useCollapsiblePanel
result: taken as the page's own behaviour rather than a demonstration, because find-in-page opening the entry that holds the phrase is right for a documentation page; the section now says so, since nothing about it is visible until someone searches

decision: A closed panel proves nothing to a markup test
why: the claim was going to be pinned by rendering one and reading the attribute back
evidence: a closed accordion panel renders no content at all on the server, with or without the prop, so neither the attribute nor the words are there to assert
result: the test was deleted rather than weakened into something trivially true, and the file says where the evidence actually is

decision: An unselected tab panel is gone unless it is asked to stay
why: the table offers to keep one, and nothing said what happens without that, so a reader could not tell whether the prop changes anything
evidence: on a fresh load the tabs hold three tabs and one panel; rendered without the prop the other panel's words are absent, and with it they are there
result: checked in the markup rather than demonstrated on a page: those panels are one line each and would keep nothing worth keeping, so passing it there would show a reader nothing

decision: A menu item that stays open on click is documented and not demonstrated
why: the note says false keeps the menu open, for an item that toggles something, and nothing on any page passes it
evidence: the kit's part is verified — MenuItem spreads its props onto the primitive, and Base UI threads closeOnClick into the item's common props — but the behaviour itself was not driven
result: no demonstration was added: the overlays page holds no state, and a toggle item there would pretend to control something the page does not have, which is worse than a note nobody has watched work

decision: The eight classes the sheet writes by hand are now held from both sides
why: every rule reads tv slots, so one of these left behind after its last consumer went would be valid CSS shipped to every consumer and drawn on nothing
evidence: all eight are drawn today; adding a dead one to the sheet reports it, and mistyping pk-noise in a slot is already reported by the compile rule against the variant object that wrote it
result: the rule refuses a utility that shares the name, so bg-pk-paper does not answer for the pk-paper recipe

decision: The readme said the rim sweep runs on a scroll timeline
why: it groups the feed's entry animation and the rim sweep as both switched off by name because a duration clamp cannot govern a scroll timeline
evidence: only pk-rise uses animation-timeline; the rim sweeps are driven by time and are named in the reduced-motion block for a different reason, which the sheet's own comment already got right
result: the paragraph now separates the two: one is a timeline, the others are clamped sweeps that are turned off because a sweep at a millisecond is still a sweep

decision: Eight components took a props type with no name
why: a consumer wrapping one had to write React.ComponentProps of a div and guess the element, which stops being true the moment the component draws a different one
evidence: four parts of the receipt, two of the accordion, a menu shortcut and a dialog footer; Receipt in the same file already exported a name for exactly that shape, so the surface disagreed with itself
result: all eight are named and exported, and a rule asks whether the type a component takes is a name the entry exports rather than whether an XProps exists for every X, because the text roles rightly share one TextProps

decision: The tv wrapper's claim was already proved, against the real stock merge
why: the readme says the stock merge drops a size when a slot also sets a colour, and that the configured one keeps both, which nothing obviously held
evidence: tv.test.ts imports the real tailwind-variants tv and asserts it returns only the colour, and pins FONT_SIZES against the sheet in both directions
result: nothing to fix; the suspicion that it might only test the configured one was wrong

decision: Two rules were written that another file already owned
why: index.test.ts was never read before adding to the entry's guards, and it already asks whether every exported component is rendered on a page and whether every declared props type reaches the entry
evidence: it reads the same Tabs.Tab = Tab mappings to resolve a compound part, so the machinery was rebuilt as well as the rule; both copies agreed, which is how a second owner stays invisible
result: the duplicates are gone and each question has one owner again; what survived is the one genuinely new question, whether a component takes a props type with no name at all

decision: A page could name a token the sheet never declared and nothing noticed
why: nine rules in that file read the components and the pages together; the oldest one, which checks every prefix-pk-name against the theme, still read the components alone
evidence: put bg-pk-nonexistent on a page slot and the whole suite stayed green — the utility compiles to nothing, so the element loses its background in silence
result: widened to the same surface as its neighbours, and the planted token is now named against its page

decision: No rule in the suite can pass on empty input
why: a rule that reads nothing reports nothing and looks the same as a rule that found nothing, which is the worst failure a guard has
evidence: every file guards its own readers — the theme suite pins five counts, the render suite pins eighty-five components, the entry, variants, utilities and showcase suites each pin theirs
result: the crude first sweep flagged fifty-one tests, nearly all of them unit controls with literal data or covered by a guard living in another test in the same file

decision: Every page sat against the rail on a wide screen
why: each caps its own measure at 880, and a wide main left that column hard against the rail with six hundred pixels of nothing beside it, which reads as a page that failed to load its right half
evidence: measured at 1680: main 1470 wide, content 880, all of the slack on one side; centred it is 295 either way, and at 1180, 1024 and 390 nothing moves because the column already fills the width
result: the shell centres what it is given rather than eight pages each centring themselves, because the shell is where the layout decision lives and the eight strings were identical

decision: The pages' own slots stay outside the compile check, deliberately
why: Tailwind's oxide Scanner can be handed the page files and would give the exact candidates, so the boundary is closeable
evidence: it is a transitive dependency here, and its extractor is deliberately over-inclusive: every prop name and word of prose comes back as a candidate, so the check would need a filter proved not to be noise
result: not taken twice now; the browser tour already covers every class the pages render, and this is written down so it stops being revisited

decision: The design note pointed at a route file that is gone
why: it shows what a consumer writes and names app/routes/data.tsx, which became readouts.tsx earlier today; the readme was corrected then and this was not
evidence: the rule added for the readme reads one file, so it went on reporting the docs clean while a second document was stale
result: widened to every document in the package, and putting the old name back names the file that holds it

decision: The design note's other claims all hold
why: it records the counts and colours measured from the source POC and shows the text roles as code, any of which could have drifted
evidence: the four roles it prints match text.tsx exactly, and meta at 400 weight, 11px and 0.005em matches the sheet; the token values it quotes describe the POC it counted rather than this kit, so they are history and cannot drift
result: nothing else to fix there; the ten composites it lists all exist, which the export rules already hold

decision: A research note credited Base UI with forty-eight primitives beside its own list of thirty-eight
why: the number appears three times and the enumeration under it names thirty-eight component subpaths, so the document disagreed with itself
evidence: counted the package's own exports: thirty-eight components, plus six helpers of which the note lists five
result: corrected in all three places; the enumeration was right and only the number was wrong, which is why it went unnoticed

decision: A pinned dependency version had drifted
why: a research note records the version it read a package at, which is what lets someone reopen the finding; it said tailwind-variants 3.3.1
evidence: installed is 3.2.2
result: a rule now reads every version a document pins for a dependency this package has, and putting the old number back names the document; a version recorded for something surveyed and never installed stays history, because there is nothing to read it against

decision: The version rule read only the runtime dependencies
why: the router is pinned in a research note and lives in devDependencies, so the one correct pin of the four was the one nothing guarded
evidence: widened to both kinds; changing the router's number in the note now names the document, which it did not before
result: four versions are pinned across the documents, three of them installed here and one surveyed and never installed

decision: The navigation note's citations all hold
why: it cites five router exports by name and line in a source file, which is the most fragile kind of claim a note can make
evidence: createRouteMask at 263, RouteMask at 217, ToMaskOptions at 157, InferMaskTo at 321, all exact against the installed 1.170.32, whose src does ship; its statements about this package are right too — eight flat routes, no canvas, no camera
result: one imprecision fixed: the last pair was cited as one line and they are at 321 and 322

decision: A variant table can no longer offer a prop that comes from state
why: Api reads a component's tv object, which cannot tell a prop from the state Base UI hands to className; except exists for that and nothing made sure it was used, and a misspelt entry excepts nothing in silence
evidence: two components fill a variant from state — the toggle group's pressed and the switch's checked — and the one with a table already excepts its key, so the rule is clean today
result: it reads the state keys out of the components rather than a list, so a new one is covered the moment it is written; removing the except from the page names it

decision: Four counts a reader sees were typed and not derived
why: the sparkline's accessible label states its span and a rule holds it to the fixture, while the visible label beside it said sixty-four weeks as a literal, and two pages said three panes the same way
evidence: changing the fixture to fifty-two weeks made the rule name the accessible label twice and say nothing about the two visible ones
result: derived instead of guarded: the visible text now reads the fixture's own length, so it cannot say a different number from the label beside it

decision: The fixtures hold no other stated fact
why: a number can be wrong in a fixture without any component being wrong, and the pages print several
evidence: the commit total and its week count were already derived; the only other literal is a zero beside an empty series, which is true by construction; the activity grid is generated from today's date, so it always ends now, which is right for it
result: nothing else to fix; searching for counts of entries, rows, days, readings and the rest turned up only the four now derived

decision: The compile check reads the stylesheet the app ships
why: the check builds its own picture of the sheet, and a plugin option or an extra import it does not reproduce would make it measure something else
evidence: the config passes the Tailwind plugin no options, the entry is two imports and nothing more, and both resolve to the files the plugin loads
result: the model was already faithful; the gap was on the other side, in which classes get built

decision: The pages wrote a hundred and fifty classes the compile check never built
why: the reason on record was that a page slot cannot be told from any other string in a file, and that is no longer true: a string inside a tv call is a class the same way an exported variant object's is
evidence: a planted bg-pk-nonexistent on the widgets page is now named against that page; none of the hundred and fifty was dead
result: the block reader counts parens to the matching close and steps over quoted spans, so an arbitrary value carrying its own parens cannot end a block early

decision: Nine components could stop being exported without a rule noticing
why: the coverage guard asked for more than thirty owners against forty tv calls in src
evidence: dropping keycapVariants from the entry took the count to thirty-nine
result: the guard answers to the count of tv calls; counted as objects, not owners, because ownership is first-wins and one component writes no class an earlier one had not claimed

decision: The activity grid drew three cells with the class "undefined"
why: its five colours sat in a plain array outside the tv block, indexed by a level that counts bounds cleared, and the thresholds prop takes any number of bounds
evidence: rendering it with six bounds put class="... undefined" on three cells in the markup
result: the scale is a tone variant across the cell and swatch slots, a level indexes it, and bounds past the last colour land on it

decision: The legend showed five bands over a plot that could only reach three
why: the fixture's busy season peaked in the older half of the year and a grid shows the last half, measured back from today, so the top colour could never come into view
evidence: the last hundred and eighty-two days topped out at eight against a bound of ten; eighteen busier days all sat outside the window
result: the season peaks inside the window now; both grids draw all five bands, and the rule reads each grid's own days, weeks and thresholds off its tag

decision: The kit's lab app had no launch entry
why: every other app in the repo starts by name and this one did not, so browser work here began by hand each time
evidence: starting it by name opened the lab on 3400 and the readouts page answered
result: one entry in .claude/launch.json, port 3400

decision: The sheet carries its own source wherever a consumer's stylesheet lives
why: the README's one setup line rests on it, and nothing had driven it from outside this package
evidence: compiling a stylesheet in a temporary directory that only names the two imports still resolved the source to this package's src, with an absolute base
result: the mechanism holds; the extent was the problem, which the next row covers

decision: @source "." shipped the kit's own test controls to every consumer
why: the kit ships source, so everything the scan reaches becomes a rule in a consumer's stylesheet, and sixteen of the fifty-nine files it read were tests
evidence: Tailwind's own scanner over that source returned 2475 candidates including bg-white, text-zinc-400 and focus-visible:ring-offset-pk-ground, the last being a class one of these rules exists to forbid
result: narrowed to ./components with a negated glob for the tests beside them: 40 files, no test, 1454 candidates, every planted control gone and every kit class kept — supersedes the extent recorded on 2026-09-09

decision: My first matcher for that rule was vacuous
why: it treated a bare "." as a filename rather than a directory, so the scanned set came back empty and the no-tests assertion passed on nothing
evidence: putting the old @source back made the rule fail with an empty list instead of naming the sixteen test files
result: fixed to read a pattern as a directory unless it globs; the rule then names all sixteen, which is the count the real scanner reports

decision: The lab looked through the decision log for classes
why: Tailwind reads the whole package when the entry does not say otherwise, so a 550-row prose log and the test files were both class sources, and the log grows every session
evidence: the built sheet held bg-white, text-zinc-400 and ring-offset-pk-ground, and px-9 and translate-x-[3px] appear in the log as prose
result: two negations in app/styles.css: 57.8 kB from 60.6, every real class kept, and ground, font, card and radius all unchanged

decision: Every page holds at 375 pixels with nothing overflowing sideways
why: the shell was rebuilt for narrow width earlier and no page had been measured against it since
evidence: all eight routes report zero overflow, each with a 900px element planted and caught on that same route before the zero was believed
result: nothing to fix

decision: Three browser probes of mine timed out and one leaked
why: timers are throttled while the pane is hidden, so a settle loop takes far longer than its nominal delay, and a probe that dies mid-call leaves its element in the page
evidence: a leftover 900px div made four routes report 545px of overflow that was mine, and the run that reported them could not catch its own control
result: scrollWidth reads straight after an insert, so no waiting was needed at all; the sweep now plants, reads and removes in one synchronous block per route

decision: A bare track was announced as a slider on 62 and nothing else
why: Slider drew Base UI's Label only when given one, and that label is what names both the group and the input, so turning the label off took the name with it
evidence: the browser's own name computation returned null for that one control while the other five returned intensity, zoom, range and gain; the caption beside it is a styled span the control cannot see
result: Base UI's guidance is aria-label on each thumb, and the root needs it too for the group; the type now takes label or aria-label and refuses both, since a label sets aria-labelledby and outranks the other

decision: Every control on every page says what it is
why: the kit gives each chart a label for a reader who cannot see it, and no page had been read against that care
evidence: 163 elements across eight routes, none unnamed, with an unnamed button planted and caught on the last route before the zero was believed
result: one defect found and fixed, the bare track; Base UI's own hidden inputs are aria-hidden with tabindex -1 and are correctly outside the count

decision: A rule cannot see how a drawn label names its control
why: Base UI's label registers its id after mount, so server markup carries no aria-labelledby
evidence: the rule asserted it and failed while the browser showed the link on all five labelled tracks
result: the rule holds what static markup can prove — no aria-label where a label is drawn — and the browser half is written beside it

decision: The overlays say what they are, and so does everything inside them
why: the page sweep reads what is drawn, and a menu or a dialog draws nothing until it opens, so the surface most likely to hide an unnamed control was the one surface not read
evidence: all five opened and named themselves — two popovers, a nested one, an alert and a menu — with nothing unnamed inside; an unnamed button planted in the open menu was caught and a named one was not
result: nothing to fix

decision: An open popup is the one with data-open, not the first in the DOM
why: every popup on the page stays mounted with data-ending-style because the exit transition never runs in this pane, so five dialogs sit in the DOM at once
evidence: two popovers reported the same name and looked like a lookup reading the wrong element; they are two popovers about the same subject, and aria-controls off the trigger had picked the right one all along
result: use the trigger's aria-controls, or data-open; never a bare querySelector for the role

decision: The two keyboard promises the kit makes itself are kept
why: Base UI owns the keys everywhere else, but the grid and the deck are the kit's own, and each states its keys in aria-keyshortcuts where nothing had ever driven them
evidence: the grid moved a week on left and right and a day on up and down, landing on the right weekday each time; the deck settled a card per arrow with the counter falling four to zero, then dropped its shortcuts and its tab stop and said inbox clear
result: nothing to fix; the first run looked like a broken ArrowDown and was the grid ending on today, a Thursday, with no Friday to move to

decision: Nothing held the kit to the contrast ratio WCAG asks for
why: every contrast rule checked a ratio the kit states somewhere, so a pair nobody wrote a number beside was checked by nothing, and 1.4.3 asks 4.5:1 of all body text
evidence: a browser sweep of the drawn pages found none below, tightest 4.95, but that answers only for the pairs someone has built
result: the rule reads every colour written as text and holds it to every ground it can land on; the four inks whose names say where they belong go against that ground instead, and the tile answers to both stops of its gradient the way paper already did

decision: Reading a painted ratio means letting the browser composite it
why: the kit paints text in oklab, display-p3 and half-alpha forms that a hand-rolled parser would have to reimplement, and reimplementing colour is how a measurement becomes wrong quietly
evidence: a 1x1 canvas painted ground then ink and read back as sRGB bytes returned exactly 21.00 for white on black and exactly 128 for half-alpha white on black
result: used for the sweep only; the rule itself is static, and a gradient ground cannot be sampled this way, so those are counted apart rather than guessed at

decision: The focus ring was the only non-text mark held to 3:1
why: 1.4.11 asks it of whatever identifies a control and whatever tells one state from another, and for a switch or a slider that is the knob and the track, neither of which was checked
evidence: the knob reads 18 to 20 against every seat and 13 to 15 against the track at rest, and the two states are 8 to 9 apart
result: rules for both, with the alphas read out of the components so changing one moves the number; setting the off track to 0.9 alpha made all three fail

decision: A consumer importing the stylesheet gets the classes, executed rather than argued

decision: A variants object that does not pair with a component leaves the sweep in silence

decision: The two least-read test files claim only what they check

decision: A zero ceiling is the division the arithmetic file names and never gave

decision: A rule promised the slots and only checked the type

decision: My first version of that check reported forty components that were fine

decision: The typechecker caught a line of mine the tests could not

decision: Twenty-six floors run before the rule they guard, and four of them are tight

decision: That reordering is a convention, not a fix, and is worth saying so

evidence: the sharp case was the rail, where a floor of eight fired on a legitimate ninth route and hid the page that was missing; that one was fixed by lowering the floor to three

decision: The rail tells a reader which page they are on

evidence: the floor is meant to catch a reader that matched nothing, not to restate the current number, so it is now three rather than eight and the comparison reports
result: worth remembering wherever a floor sits beside a set comparison, which is most rules in this suite

decision: The six form controls moved to a page of their own

decision: The two pages were looked at rather than only measured

decision: Four tables I added this session printed the words "no variants" to a reader

why: every doc-accuracy rule in this suite reads a table that Api or Props renders, and neither had been read this session
evidence: Api reads variants and defaults straight off the tv object so it cannot fall behind a component; Props types each row name as keyof the props type, so a renamed prop fails the build, and its hand-written fallbacks are held by the stated-default rule

decision: A component earns a test by working something out, and that is a rule now

decision: Every variant table on the pages offers only props a consumer can pass

evidence: all 23 tables check out; a first pass flagged toggle-group's look and separator's orientation, and both are real — one declared outright, one owned by the Base UI primitive underneath, which is a third way a variant reaches a consumer beyond VariantProps
result: nothing to fix; four components with variants have no table and are right not to, since tone, active and held are all values they work out themselves

decision: A variant the component computes itself is invisible to the rule that guards tables
why: stateShownAsProp finds a variant filled from Base UI state by matching key: state.key, and the activity grid's tone, the layout preview's active and the swipe deck's held are filled from the component's own arithmetic instead

decision: The readme quoted a terminal that could not run

decision: The foundations swatches cannot show a token other than the one beside them

decision: My control for the readme rule passed on nothing twice

evidence: caught by the one case that expected a failure; the fixture now asserts what the pattern found before it asserts what the rule says about it

decision: NumberField, and the drag is the reason it is here

decision: A synthetic pointer drag needs movementX set explicitly
why: the scrub area sets data-scrubbing on pointerdown, so it looked live, and twenty pointermoves changed nothing
evidence: Base UI reads movementX, which a default PointerEvent leaves at zero; setting it in the event init made the same drag move the value

decision: The controls page holds with the combobox on it, at both widths

decision: The popup look has one owner now, and the select borrows it

decision: Combobox, which is the palette the kit's own bindings advertise
why: the bindings fixture lists command-K for a palette and nothing in the kit could draw one
evidence: driven with real keystrokes: typing pass opens the list and narrows six commands to raster pass, and a query matching none of them shows the empty line instead of closing on an empty box

decision: My first combobox typechecked, rendered, and could not be opened
why: I read the anatomy and not an example, so I wrapped the items in the List myself and put Empty inside it
evidence: Base UI filters the root's items and hands each survivor to a render function on List; a written-out list is narrowed by nothing, and the popup stayed shut through every query

decision: A synthetic input event cannot drive a Base UI field
why: the native value setter plus an input event is the usual way, and it left aria-expanded false through three queries, which read as a broken component
evidence: the same queries typed as real keystrokes opened the popup and filtered it; the DOM value had been moving while React's state had not
result: drive a controlled field with computer type, not with dispatched events; and focus arming is cleared by every navigate, so focus the element from JS first

decision: The type scale is px throughout, so a reader's own font size does nothing

evidence: read the sheet: every --text-pk-* is a px value, and so are the fifteen bare sizes in slots

decision: The fifteen bare sizes in slots are deliberate, not slips
why: each duplicates a rung's value while getting none of its line-height, letter-spacing or weight, which looks like opting out of the type system by accident
evidence: six of the fifteen match two rungs at once, so a bare number is the clearer of the two; and the ones measured in the browser all set their own leading, which is why the rung was not used
result: nothing to fix; the rule that holds a size to the ladder is right to check the value and not the name

decision: Reduced motion was checked for animations and not for transitions

evidence: the kit transitions transform, translate, height, width, left, top and grid-template-columns, none of which are in that list, so all of them stop; adding transform to the list made the new rule name it
result: two rules — nothing in the list may move, and every property a slot names outright must already be answered for by the list or be motion

decision: Which colours still fade under reduced motion is taste, and wider than the list
why: Tailwind's transition-colors reaches outline-color, fill, stroke and the gradient variables, none of which the block keeps
evidence: read off a live element: transition-colors resolves to ten properties and the block keeps four of them
result: left as it is — a fill that jumps instead of fading is the harmless direction, and the promise being kept is that nothing moves

decision: The reduced state cannot be observed in this environment
why: neither browser tool emulates prefers-reduced-motion, so the cascade was read rather than watched
evidence: the block is in the CSSOM as one media rule with both of its inner rules intact, and matchMedia reports false, so it is parsed and not applying
result: the rules are static and read the sheet's own text; what a reduced-motion user actually sees is unwitnessed here

decision: The controls page still holds with four new controls on it

evidence: 375 pixels with nothing overflowing, a 900px element planted and caught; and the select's popup, which is a ground no earlier sweep had reached, reads 12.01 on its rows and 16.58 on the chosen one
result: nothing to fix

decision: A select root is not a root that waits to be opened

evidence: it always draws a hidden input carrying its value into a form, so the rule that lists the silent roots refused it

decision: The grounds section reads its count off the array rather than stating it

result: the ring sweep found the number field; nothing else, and the sweep cannot live in the suite because :focus-visible needs a focused window

decision: What a popup holds was never in any sweep, because a closed popup draws nothing
why: the page sweeps only ever saw the triggers, so the select list, the combobox list, the menu, the popover and the dialog had never been read at all
evidence: each was opened on its own and read: every item is named, every item carries its highlight, the popover and the dialog both name themselves, and the combobox hands each option an id
result: the combobox opens on typing rather than on a click, so it needed a real keystroke; a click on role=combobox reached the select, whose trigger carries the same role

decision: The readme was a day behind the kit it introduces
why: it counted eight routes and listed the controls without the six the forms page was built from
evidence: the rules only ever asked the other way round — that a route the readme names exists, and that the module counts are right — so a page and six modules could arrive and leave no mark on it
result: the routes now read nine and name the forms page, the controls are split into controls and forms, and both directions are checked; on the readme as it was committed all three new assertions fail

decision: The design note quoted three of the seven text roles as if that were the block
why: the quote rule reads the readme and nothing else, and the note writes its file paths out in full, which the pattern did not accept
evidence: the block in the note stops after label, kind, meta and readout; text.tsx has had title, display and prose for as long as the pages have shown them
result: the quote is the whole block now, the rule reads the note as well, and the note says its source html is at the repository root rather than in this package

decision: Both research notes counted a kit that has grown since
why: the readme's counts are checked and the notes' are not, and a note states its counts in digits where the readme spells them
evidence: the committed notes say 39 modules twice and eight flat routes once; the kit has 46 modules and the app has nine routes
result: each count is read out of the same directory the readme's is, in words or digits, across every document listed for the version rule

decision: A placeholder was under the floor on the fill its own input paints
why: every contrast rule reads a flat token, and a translucent fill is a ground the kit paints itself
evidence: the combobox placeholder measured 4.40:1 in the browser inside a card, and the same maths in the suite reported seven pairs under 4.5, the worst 3.96 on the hover fill; the faint ink is the floor on a surface, and a fill lightens the surface under it
result: the placeholder takes the dim ink, and the soft tone answers a pointer on its edge instead of lightening its fill, which is what the outline tone already does; measured again in the browser at 5.03 and 5.66

decision: The recess token would have been the other fix, and was not taken
why: an input is a cut opening and the theme declares a colour for one, which would darken the ground under the ink rather than brighten the ink
evidence: recess is #040505 against a card at #0e0f11, so every input would become the darkest thing on the page — a redesign of a whole control family, not a repair of a ratio
result: left alone; the token still has no consumer, which is worth a look when someone owns that decision

decision: Every word on every page, against the ground it is actually painted on
why: the suite reads tokens and the pages composite them, so a colour can clear on paper and fail in place
evidence: 1425 pieces of text across nine pages, each read against the whole stack of backgrounds above it, with a deliberately thin pair planted each time and caught each time; the only reports are the receipt, whose paper is a gradient that a background-colour read cannot see, and whose ratios the suite already checks against both of its stops
result: nothing else is under its floor; a sweep of this kind cannot read a gradient ground, so read paper from the rule that owns it rather than from the page

decision: A hovered nav row put its trailing text on a lightened ground
why: the placeholder rule covered the input alone, and five other components paint a fill under text
evidence: generalised, the rule reported one pair the browser sweep could not have reached: a nav row lightens itself on hover while its trail keeps the faint ink, which is 4.40:1 on a card and 4.49 on a sunken one
result: the trail brightens with the row, a step behind the label, on hover and on focus alike; the rule now reads which ink applies under the state that paints the fill, so an ink a hover replaces is not counted against it

decision: What sits under what is read from the tv block, not assumed
why: a fill is a ground for the text above it, and a component decides which text that is
evidence: a first cut called every ink in a slots object a tenant of every fill and reported the feed's faint notes against a chip they never sit on; a second read the slot strings loose, so the trail's plain ink and its hover ink landed in different strings and the repair looked like it had not worked
result: classes are gathered by the key that owns them, a root is under every ink and a leaf under its own, and two values of one variant are never paired — the badge's quiet ink against the neutral fill is the case that names

decision: A disabled slider and a disabled collapsible looked exactly like live ones
why: the contrast rule skips the inks an inactive control wears, which is only fair if the control really is inactive and really looks it
evidence: eleven components fade to 40% and stop taking a pointer; asking every export to render with disabled and reading the classes back showed two that take the prop and draw nothing for it
result: the slider fades whole and the collapsible fades its trigger and not its panel, since an open panel still has to be readable; the disabled slider is on the controls page, at 0.4 opacity and pointer-events none, and its range input carries the disabled attribute so it is out of the tab order as well

decision: A container is asked with the part it holds
why: rendering a control with disabled and reading its classes is the only way to see a treatment that arrives by composition, which reading the file cannot
evidence: childless, a toolbar, a field, a radio group, an accordion and a toggle group all reported: each puts the fade on the part it holds rather than on the root it draws
result: each has a representative part in the fixture map, so what a reader would see is what the rule reads; the number field passed that way before the others, which is what named the shape

decision: A disabled field held a button that was fully live
why: Base UI hands its own form controls the field's state, and a button is not one of its form controls
evidence: measured in place: the label was at 0.4 and the input was off and greyed, while the button beside them was at full opacity, took a pointer and kept its cursor — under a greyed label saying the whole thing was off
result: the page passes disabled to that button; the field now reads off from end to end, and a rule asks every page the same question

decision: Which controls a field turns off is asked of the kit, not listed
why: a rule that names the form controls by hand is a list that rots, and the answer is already in the components
evidence: each export is rendered with disabled to see whether it answers at all, then rendered inside a disabled field to see whether it takes the state from context; the input and the field's own label do, and the button does not, which is the whole distinction
result: the first cut of this reported nothing because the render helper was never imported in that file and every call threw into the catch — the planted control is what said so, and the same shape is why every sweep here plants one

decision: A label on a disabled field leads nowhere, which is what it should do
why: the label keeps taking a pointer while the control beside it does not, so a click could have moved focus into something dead
evidence: clicked both: a live field's label moves focus to its input, and a disabled field's label leaves focus where it was
result: nothing to change; cursor default and no focus move is the whole treatment, and it is right

decision: The sheet stills what the readme says it stills
why: two claims about reduced motion sat in the readme with nothing reading them against the file
evidence: the animations a duration cannot govern are derived rather than listed — an animation on a view timeline takes its progress from the scroll position — and the sheet has exactly one, which the block does name
result: the rule also holds the transition list to colour, shadow and opacity, so transform or height rejoining it is a failure rather than a quiet change

decision: Base UI unmounts on getAnimations, not on transitionend
why: whether a closing panel still unmounts when the sheet removes its transition decides if reduced motion strands an open panel
evidence: useAnimationsFinished waits on each animation's finished promise and calls back at once when there are none, so a property the sheet stops transitioning leaves nothing to wait for
result: reduced motion cannot strand a panel; what a frozen preview pane strands is different — its animations exist and never finish, which is why the two look alike and are not

decision: A colour nothing paints with is an orphan, and colours were exempt
why: the rule for dead exports maps one prefix to one namespace, and a colour is written under a dozen, so it skipped every colour the sheet declares
evidence: asked the other way it answers: a colour is painted when a file writes any utility that resolves to it, or when the sheet uses it in a recipe of its own; run against the sheet as it stood it reported exactly one, which is what a hand sweep had found
result: the aliases are dropped before reading, since a line republishing a token under a prefix is not a use of it, and a utility is resolved at its own -pk- rather than by the name it ends with — border-pk-pane-line is not a use of pk-line

decision: The recess colour is gone rather than kept for a design that may want it
why: it was declared, aliased, taught on the foundations page as one of six grounds, and used to draw nothing anywhere
evidence: the same colour was the other candidate for the input fill this morning and was rejected as a redesign, which is what left it dead; keeping a token because a future change might want it is the shim this repo does not keep
result: three lines: the declaration, the alias and the page's row; the page now says five grounds because that count reads the array, and the browser resolves --pk-recess to nothing. Bringing it back is those three lines, beside the change that needs it

decision: A prefix the map has never heard of is a failure, not an exemption
why: the rule that checks a utility against the tokens the sheet declares reads a map of prefixes, and skips anything the map lacks, so a whole family can be checked by nothing
evidence: the kit writes twelve prefixes and the map held ten of them: inset-ring on the scroll area and rounded-b on two page trays were both invisible, and a typo under either compiles to no rule and loses the ring or the corner in silence
result: inset-ring is in the map, a side is stripped so one entry covers a family — rounded-b reads the tray radius — and an unknown prefix now fails; both of the two name real tokens, which the reference rule confirmed the moment it could see them

decision: The text prefix reads two namespaces, which is exact only while they are disjoint
why: a reference under text- passes if either a size or a colour declares it, so a name declared as both would mean two things and the rule could not say which
evidence: they are disjoint today: thirty-one names written under text-, every one of them a size or a colour and none of them both
result: the disjointness is now the rule rather than an assumption, so a colour named like a size fails on the day it is declared instead of quietly making a utility ambiguous

decision: Nine pages at the width of a phone, which nothing had ever measured
why: every sweep so far ran at 900 pixels, and a component with a fixed width fails narrow rather than wide
evidence: 375 pixels, all nine pages, a 900px element planted on each and caught on each: nothing extends past the viewport that is not inside something that scrolls, and the document never scrolls sideways
result: looked at the densest page as well as measured it — the nav wraps to a row, the marks wrap, the tables stack and the terminal keeps its own scroller

decision: The tooltip rule promised more than it asked
why: its name says every trigger says what its tooltip says, and it only asked whether an aria-label was present at all
evidence: a trigger reading aria-label=queries beside a tooltip reading 2.1M served would have passed, which is the one failure the label exists to prevent
result: the label is now compared with the tooltip's words, punctuation out of both since a label writes commas where the tooltip prints a middot; both triggers on the page already held, so this closes a hole rather than reporting one

decision: A tooltip is unreachable on a phone, and the readme now says so
why: the readme explains why a tooltip's words must be on the trigger for a screen reader, and said nothing about the reader who can see but cannot hover
evidence: measured with touch emulated at 375px: (hover: hover) is false, so every hover utility is inert, and Base UI's hover path runs only for a mouse-like pointer
result: the guidance is to keep a tooltip for a hint that repeats the trigger and put anything that has to be seen in the layout; the overlays demo keeps its two, because a page about tooltips has to draw one

decision: Reading every test name against its own assertions found three that did not match
why: one rule was caught overclaiming by accident, which said nothing about how many others did
evidence: two contrast sweeps asserted only that their report was empty, so an empty seat list would have passed them on nothing; a toggle test was named for a fill the unpressed item does not wear, which is true of the segmented look and false of the chips, and no assertion touched the half that was wrong
result: both sweeps now count their pairs before reading them, and the toggle test is named and written for what the two looks do — pressing changes the fill, in one case from none and in the other from a six percent ink

decision: The type section's roles were listed by hand, and the readout was not among them
why: the rule reads text.tsx for each role's token, then matched the page with a written-out list of six role names
evidence: the readout row added this morning was never checked, and the count pinned beside it said six, so the hole looked like the answer
result: the pattern is built from the roles the component declares and the pin is now that every declared role states its size on the page, so a role added to text.tsx joins the rule instead of slipping past it

decision: The last seven test files, read the same way, gave three loops that could check nothing
why: a loop over computed data asserts nothing when the data is empty, and reads exactly like a loop that passed
evidence: the weekday check walks the grid's own columns, the width check walks the widths a helper draws and the finite check walks the points a plot returns; each would have gone green if its helper returned an empty list, which is the regression each exists to catch
result: each counts what it is about to read first — a hundred and seventy days, seven widths, ten points — so an empty result fails where it used to pass; sixteen files are now read, and the names of the other four files' tests match what they assert

decision: Two rules that look independent are not, and both files now say so
why: after a session of adding guards, the question worth asking is which of them can fail on their own
evidence: measured by mutation rather than by reading: a page given bg-pk-nonexistent fails both the token rule and the compile rule, and one given size-16x fails only the compile rule; no change was found that fails only the token rule
result: the token rule stays, for the two things it does differently — it names the token and the file where the other says a class built nothing, and it reads sources without building a stylesheet, so it still answers when the build is what broke; deleting a guard whose only fault is redundancy is how coverage disappears the day the other one is narrowed

decision: The suite costs nothing to run, so nothing is worth pruning for speed
why: the case for removing an overlapping rule is usually its cost
evidence: every assertion in every file totals about 360 milliseconds; the wall clock is import time, and the two slowest files are the two that render components
result: cost is off the table as a reason; overlap is now recorded where it exists rather than acted on

decision: The two remaining pairs are independent, in both directions each
why: reading is what got the first pair wrong, so the other two were owed the same treatment rather than an argument
evidence: four mutations, each reverted: dropping a caption from a page fails only the affordance rule, removing the neutral badge fails only the tabled-value rule, painting the aurora with another colour fails only the colour rule, and taking the ping off the status dot fails only the mechanism rule
result: all four rules earn their place; the suite has one subsumed pair, named in both its files, and no others among the four asked

decision: Mutation is how a rule is read here, not argument
why: a rule's coverage is a claim about what breaks it, and the only way to know is to break something
evidence: each mutation went in with Edit and came out with the inverse Edit before the next one; git status was read afterwards to prove the tree was clean
result: the pattern is worth keeping: one change at a time, run the suite, record the names that fail, revert before the next

decision: The four rules written today each catch the regression they were written for
why: a rule proved only by its own fixture has never met the sources it guards
evidence: four more mutations, each reverted: the slider's disabled mark taken off fails only the disabled sweep, the row's trail left faint fails only the painted-grounds rule, a tooltip trigger stripped back to one word fails only the tooltip comparison, and divide-pk-line on the separator fails only the prefix rule
result: the last one is the interesting one — it is a valid class that compiles, so the wider compile rule stays green, which is the case the prefix rule exists for and the one that proves it is not another copy of it

decision: The three rules whose derivation is most indirect all catch their regression
why: each resolves through a mapping or a second read, which is where a plausible regression slips past
evidence: a part exported and drawn nowhere fails the rendered-on-a-page rule, and the props-type rule as well because the mutation forgot its type — both correct; a table of a variants object with no variants fails the nothing-to-list rule; a helper added to the avatar with no test beside it fails the has-a-test rule
result: thirteen rules are now proved against the sources rather than against a fixture; every page in the kit draws each component at least twice, so the regression this suite would actually see is an export nobody demonstrates rather than a demonstration removed

decision: The four rules that read documents each catch a document going stale
why: a document drifts silently, which is the whole reason those rules exist and the reason a fixture proves least about them
evidence: four mutations, each reverted: a version pin moved by one patch fails the pin rule, a class changed inside the readme's quoted block fails the quote rule, eight flat routes in the navigation note fails the route-count rule, and forty-four modules in the runtime note fails the module-count rule
result: seventeen rules are now proved against the real files

decision: The route-reference rule cannot see a splat name, and that is load-bearing
why: widening a pattern looks like an improvement until it reports the thing it was written to leave alone
evidence: the navigation note tells the story of app/routes/w.$.tsx, a lab route removed on purpose, and says so in the same sentence; the pattern reads a plain file name, so the story stands and a genuine stale pointer is still caught
result: written above the rule, because the next reader to notice the gap will otherwise close it

decision: A colour nudged by a hex digit is caught, and by which rules depends on the nudge
why: the contrast family is the largest block never proved against the sheet, and its regression is a change that looks harmless in a diff
evidence: three mutations, each reverted: darkening the faint ink a little fails the two stated-ratio rules and nothing else, because it stays above the floor; darkening the paper's foot fails only the paper pair; and a much darker accent fails five at once — the ring on every seat, the two states apart, the knob against its track, the text floor and a stated ratio
result: the floor rules and the stated-ratio rules are independent, which is the useful part: a nudge that stays legal still cannot pass, because the page and the components state numbers the sheet has to keep producing

decision: The scan boundary holds in both directions, which is the one that ships
why: the sheet's @source decides which files a consumer's build reads, so a wrong glob ships a kit whose classes do not exist downstream and whose own pages look fine
evidence: narrowed to a single component and then widened by dropping the negation on the test files: both fail the same rule, which is the one that asks what a consumer scans and asks that no test is among it
result: the highest-consequence rule in the package, now broken on purpose twice and caught twice

decision: A page dropped from the rail is caught
why: the rail is written by hand beside a routes directory that is generated
evidence: taking the forms link out fails the rule that asks the rail to offer every page and each of them once
result: the route-tree rule was left unproved on purpose: proving it means adding a route file and then removing it, and removing a repository file is not something to do for a measurement

decision: A renamed export is caught six ways, which the file had claimed and never shown
why: the entry re-exports by name, so a rename at the source leaves a binding that resolves to nothing
evidence: renaming rowVariants to rowStyles at its source fails three entry rules, two variant rules and a table rule, and stops one test file loading at all; dropping a props type from the entry fails the rule that asks every props type to reach it
result: the comment in that file said the rename had been checked by hand once; it is now a run rather than a note

decision: One branch of the entry rule cannot be reached by any single edit to the kit
why: a rule proved by its fixture and not by the sources is worth saying so about rather than counting as done
evidence: emptying the separator's base still draws, because its orientation variant does; emptying both of the field's slots still draws, because its layout variant does — every object in the kit has either a base or a default variant that carries classes, so no one edit makes one yield nothing
result: the branch keeps its fixture and this row keeps the reason; a rule that reports it in the wild needs a component gutted in several places at once, which is not a regression that arrives quietly

decision: Nothing but the two that mean to may reach for the stock tv
why: the readme states this as a rule and no rule read it, so a component could take the unconfigured merge and pass everything
evidence: dropping one name from the size list fails four rules, but importing tv from tailwind-variants in the badge failed nothing at all — 234 green with a component on the stock merge
result: the import is now checked across src and the components, with tv.ts and this test named as the two that import it on purpose; re-applying the mutation fails the new rule and nothing else

decision: The stock merge does not always drop a class, which is why the rule is about the import
why: a rule is easier to argue for when the damage is universal, and this damage is not
evidence: measured in a browser after a full reload: the badge kept both text-pk-ink-dim and text-pk-label under the stock merge, because its size happens to come last, while the pair in the tv fixture loses one — I predicted the badge would break and it did not
result: the check reads the import rather than the outcome, since the outcome depends on the order of two strings in a component nobody is thinking about while editing it

decision: The arithmetic that draws wrongly rather than loudly is caught three ways
why: a wrong division still draws a chart, which no page sweep, no typecheck and no eye reading a screenshot would question
evidence: three mutations, each reverted: holding real values up to the floor fails the test written for that very bug, a step divided by the count rather than the gaps fails the rule that the first point sits at the left edge and the last at the right, and an inverted scale fails the rule that the highest reading is drawn above the lowest
result: the floor mutation is the one worth noting: the comment beside that helper describes the bug from the day it was found, and re-introducing it fails the test named for it, so the note and the guard agree

decision: The mutation pass is finished, and every rule fires on the regression it was written for
why: a suite that has never failed on purpose is a suite nobody has read
evidence: four more mutations close it: a commit distance that no longer commits fails two swipe rules, weeks rounded up rather than down fails two grid rules, an unclamped negative share fails three breakdown rules, and a separator consuming a step of the cascade fails two ticker rules
result: every rule in the package has now been broken on purpose and caught, except three that are named with their reasons — the route tree, which would mean deleting a route file, the empty-variants branch, which no single edit reaches, and the reduced-motion sheet, which no browser here can emulate

decision: The overview board packs cleanly at every width it meets
why: the board was packed as a dense grid this morning and only ever looked at near 900 pixels
evidence: measured at 375, 760, 900, 1024 and 1440: four columns at the widest and the board caps at 880 rather than stretching, three at 1024, two at 760, one on a phone; every row fills its columns, no row is left ragged and nothing overflows at any of them
result: the case worth checking was 1024, where three columns meet cards that mostly span two — dense backfill fills it, so the odd column never leaves a hole

decision: The contact card carries a lot of air in a wide cell, and it is the owner's call
why: at 434 pixels the avatar, name, role and status take about the left half and the rest is empty, beside neighbours that are dense with figures
evidence: looked at full resolution rather than in a thumbnail: the aurora card next to it reads as deliberate quiet, and this one reads as a small card in a large seat; every prop the card takes is already passed somewhere, so there is no affordance to reach for
result: filling it would mean inventing content for a card the owner approved, so it stays; a narrower seat or more content are both design decisions rather than repairs

decision: A section said three figures and drew two
why: looking at the widgets page above 900 for the first time, where a three-column grid holds four cards and puts the fourth alone in a row
evidence: the readouts section draws two breakdowns and two metric tiles, and its line reads a language split, three figures, a terminal
result: the words are corrected rather than a third tile added: the claim is a repair, the content is the owner's composition; the overview does draw three tiles for the same subject, which is probably where the three came from

decision: This is the second free count to drift, and the boundary is exact
why: a count beside a variant key is checked and a count beside anything else is not, which is easy to forget when both read the same on the page
evidence: 2 shapes on the bars section is guarded, because shape is a variant of that component; three figures was not, because figures is not a variant of anything — the same sentence shape, one checked and one not
result: the other free counts were read by hand and hold: three series shapes draws three sparklines, two series draws two, and six on the foundations page became a length this morning; a rule for these was rejected earlier and the reason still stands

decision: A three-column grid leaves the fourth card alone above about 1180
why: the widgets page caps at 880 like the rest, so the column count only changes with the pane, and nothing had looked at it wide
evidence: the readouts grid fills three columns and puts the fourth card in a row of its own with two empty cells beside it; at 900 the same grid is two columns and the four cards sit square
result: left as it is: a fifth card or a wider minimum are both design changes, and the raggedness is a masonry row rather than a fault

decision: All nine pages hold at 1440, and the two composed by hand were read rather than measured
why: seven pages had only ever been seen at 900 and 375
evidence: nothing overflows on any of them at 1440, every page caps at 880 and centres rather than stretching; the readouts page and the layout page were looked at in full, and both read as they should — three sparklines abreast, the activity plots full width, the surface tones in rows of three, three and two
result: the eighth surface card added this morning improved that last row rather than spoiling it: seven tones packed three, three and one

decision: A raggedness check by y position reports the wrong thing
why: the sweep called nine grids ragged and the honest answer was none of them
evidence: grouping children by their y coordinate reads a props table's zero-height cells as one row, and reads the activity plot's twenty-seven day columns as a grid with twenty-seven columns and a short final week — which is what a partial week looks like and not a fault
result: a sweep that means to find a short last row has to read grid-row from the computed style, or restrict itself to grids whose children are cards; the eye is what settled it this time

decision: A reader who asks for larger text gets none, and here is what changing that costs
why: the type scale is written in pixels and has been flagged twice without a measurement to hand
evidence: demonstrated rather than argued: raising the root font size from 16 to 24 in the browser left every size on the page exactly where it was — display 21, prose 13, label and meta 11, unmoved; browser zoom still works, so this is the reader who raises the default rather than the one who zooms
result: the conversion is sixteen tokens and fifteen arbitrary sizes, and 11px becomes 0.6875rem — visually identical at a default root

decision: The reason the type conversion is the owner's is not the size of the diff
why: a mechanical rewrite that changes no pixel would ordinarily be mine to make
evidence: the foundations page teaches the scale by stating it — Display · 21px, Title · 15px, six more — and a rule checks each against the token; in rem those numbers become true only at a default root, so the page would have to say something else, and what a design system says about its own scale is a decision about the design
result: measured and left; if it is taken, the page's wording and the rule that checks it move with the tokens, or the page starts stating rem

decision: Five sliders left one alone in a row of four, and the row was mine
why: the disabled slider added this morning made five where four had filled a row exactly, which only shows above about 1200
evidence: at 1440 the grid held four tracks and put the fifth on its own with three empty cells beside it; raising the column minimum from 196 to 250 makes it three to a row, so five read as three and two
result: the narrow widths keep what they had — two abreast at 900 and one on a phone, one empty cell at the end either way — and every track is wider than it was, which a track wants more than a card does

decision: The forms page reads well wide, and the other three hold nothing that could go ragged
why: the row arithmetic that stranded a slider is worth asking of every page rather than only the one that showed it
evidence: at 1440 the forms page runs three columns: the input section fills a row exactly where at 900 it left an orphan, and the radio and select sections sit two abreast; the disclosure, overlays and foundations pages have no card grids at all, so their demos are stacks and inline rows that the overflow sweep already covered
result: the arithmetic to ask of a grid is how many cards against how many columns, at each width where the column count changes — cards divided by columns leaving one is the shape that looks like a mistake

decision: The combobox demo sits alone in a three-column row
why: one card in a row built for three leaves two thirds of it empty, which is the widest gap on the page
evidence: the section draws a single combobox because that is what there is to show; letting the card span the row would stretch a text field to 880 pixels, which is worse for the control than the gap is for the page
result: left as it is, and it is the same class as the contact card — a small card in a large seat, where filling it means inventing a second demo nobody asked for

decision: The setup the readme teaches has to be one the manifest serves
why: every rule here reads this repository's own sources, and none had read the file that decides what anyone else receives
evidence: the kit has exactly one consumer, its own lab app, which imports by package name on purpose so the documented path is the one that runs; nothing tied the readme's import lines to the exports map, so a subpath the readme taught and the manifest did not export would fail on someone else's machine first
result: the readme's specifiers are read against the exports map and every exported path is checked to exist; asking the readme for a tokens stylesheet that is not exported fails the rule, and the entry and the theme are pinned so it cannot compare nothing

decision: The package is private and exports source, so there is no build to check
why: looking for what a consumer receives, the answer is that no other package in the workspace depends on this one
evidence: exports point at src/index.ts and src/theme.css, both raw; that is right for a workspace consumer with a bundler and impossible for plain node, which is what private means here
result: nothing to fix; recorded so the next look for a publishing gap starts from the fact rather than from the assumption that one exists

decision: The API document the commit hook checks belongs to another package
why: the line printed on every commit here reads like this package's public surface being verified
evidence: the script is packages/infinite-canvas/scripts/verify-api-doc.mjs, its barrels are that package's index and scene, and it reads the repository root's docs/API.md; the counts it prints are that package's, and this one has no API document at all
result: no gap: this package documents its surface through the readme's component list, which is checked against the modules, and through pages that draw every export; said plainly because I had assumed the opposite one turn earlier

decision: A module a consumer loads may import only what the manifest promises
why: a development dependency resolves in a workspace where everything is installed and is simply absent on the machine that installs the package
evidence: the shipped modules import Base UI, d3-shape, tailwind-variants and React — three dependencies and a peer — and nothing else; a type import of the router added to the separator fails the new rule, which is what that mistake would look like
result: the pages are exempt on purpose, since the lab app ships to nobody and may reach for the router and the test runner the way any application does

decision: Nothing a consumer loads may do anything at import time but hang up its parts
why: the manifest tells a bundler that only a stylesheet has an effect, which is what lets a consumer's build drop what it does not use; a module that reached for the document would be dropped with it and the bug would appear only in a production build
evidence: the shipped modules hold exactly one kind of top-level statement, the compound parts — Tabs.List = TabsList and its twenty siblings — and the manifest's side-effect glob covers both stylesheets
result: the allowance is written as the shape of that idiom rather than as a general assignment, for the reason in the row below

decision: The first version of that rule allowed the thing it was written to catch
why: an allowance for a.b = c is an allowance for anything, which reads as a narrow exception and is not
evidence: the mutation went in and passed: globalThis.__pkKeycapLoaded = true matches a word, a dot, a word, an equals and a word as exactly as Tabs.List = TabsList does
result: the allowance now asks for capitals on all three, which is what a component assignment looks like and what a global flag does not; the rule failed the mutation on the next run

decision: The fixtures state no total by hand, so the drift I went looking for cannot happen
why: every page reads its figures from the same file, and a fixture disagreeing with its own caption would make several rules agree on a wrong number
evidence: each figure beside a series is derived from it — the commit total is a reduce, the peak a max, its week an index of, the frame a last element, the install ceiling a max — so there is nothing for a caption to contradict
result: the class of bug exists and this file is not where it lives; the counts that did drift today were words in prose, not numbers in data

decision: A ceiling two charts share has to be one both of them fit under
why: the bars clamp a share at one, so a series that outgrows its ceiling does not overflow or throw — it flattens against the top and keeps drawing
evidence: the one scale section teaches a comparison between two install series under a single ceiling taken from the larger; raising the smaller one past it fails the new rule, which is what that mistake would look like and what nothing would otherwise say
result: the rule reads the ceiling's own definition rather than a number, so it follows whichever series the page decides to take the ceiling from

decision: The generated fixture reaches every band with room to spare, and will keep doing so
why: the band rule reads that fixture as ground truth, and a generator that only just reached the top band would make the rule pass by luck
evidence: counted in the browser rather than in the data: the contributions grid draws 49, 39, 46, 36 and 17 days across its five bands, and the pages-read grid 26, 30, 22, 33 and 20 — no band is thin
result: the distribution is the same on any day it runs: the index drives the pseudo-random, and the seasonal peak sits seventy days before today whenever today is, which is what the comment beside the generator was tuned for

decision: Neither table can drop a row, so the slip worth a rule is a row that says only its name
why: every rule so far reads a page's source, and the two components all that documentation flows through had never been read for what they render — a row lost inside one would leave every source rule green and the page saying less than it claims
evidence: both tables map their input, so a drop has nowhere to happen: the browser shows 93 rows on nine pages against 93 written. Mutating the slider's label row to a name alone failed the new rule
result: the rule asks each props row for values, a fallback or a note, and floors the number of rows it reads, so a reader that finds nothing cannot pass as a page with nothing wrong

decision: A consumer who imports the theme gets every class, and has to write nothing of their own
why: I have said several times this session that it was unmeasured, and it is the one defect a consumer would see before anything else: the components arrive unstyled and nothing here would say so
evidence: turned automatic detection off in the lab entry with source(none) and built for real. A class only keycap.tsx writes was still in the stylesheet; a class only the lab writes was gone. The directive inside the shipped file did that work, and Tailwind documents @source as the way to override its node_modules rule
result: the lab now runs the consumer path and its own path at once, so the setup the pages document is the setup that was proved

decision: The lab cannot see this break, so a rule has to stand in for the consumer
why: the lab scans the whole package by itself. A class in a file outside @source still draws on these pages while a consumer gets nothing, which is a defect that looks like success from every angle available here
evidence: the rule reads the directives out of theme.css rather than naming the folder, expands them the way Tailwind does, and asks where each file holding classes sits. Narrowing the directive to one component failed it with the other 45 named
result: it also corrected the note above those directives, which said the theme read all of src and counted sixteen test files — it reads one folder, cuts six test files, and never reaches the rules that plant wrong classes on purpose

decision: The select and the combobox do draw a keyboard highlight, and I said they did not
why: I looked for the state in each file and found none, which is the wrong place to look — both take their item from the menu, the way the trigger takes its look from the input
evidence: the classes arrive by composition: menuVariants().item() carries the highlight, and select and combobox layer only what they add on top of it
result: a check for a drawn state has to read what a component renders, not what its own file writes; the file said nothing because there was nothing left to say

decision: The toolbar was the one part of the kit that drew nothing of its own
why: every page that used it passed render with a whole ghost button inside, nine times on one page. A consumer writing the plain part would get a browser default button sitting in a styled tray, and no rule here would say so
evidence: the select trigger already showed the shape: draw over the owning variant rather than a second copy of it. The toolbar button now takes tone and size from the button and defaults to ghost, which is the tone a tray wants
result: checked in the running page rather than from the types: nine native buttons in the kit's ghost ink, 28px for an icon and 24 for a small, the disabled one at four tenths and still reachable, a two pixel accent ring on real keyboard focus, and the arrows still moving the one tab stop between them

decision: A fixture that props a part up hides the very thing the rule looks for
why: the sweep handed the toolbar a button through render, so the rule that asks whether a control fades when disabled was reading the button's fade and calling it the toolbar's. The toolbar drew nothing for a year of rules and two of them were watching
evidence: the fixture now builds the bare part. Dropping the toolbar button's own classes fails both the new keyboard rule and the disabled rule that was already there — the older one had been blind only because the fixture dressed its subject
result: a container in that list is judged with its parts, so a part has to be the plain one. Anything a page would have to add to make it look right is a defect the fixture would otherwise carry

decision: A part the keyboard can reach has to draw something when it gets there
why: I nearly wrote this against each component's own file, which is the reading that called the select wrong this morning and would have called the toolbar right
evidence: it reads the rendered markup: a ring for real focus, or the highlight a menu moves in place of focus. Base UI's hidden input for form values is aria-hidden, and that is what takes it out — not its size or its clip
result: the first version passed the mutation it was written for, because rendering a toolbar button alone throws and the catch swallowed it. It only bites now that the fixture renders the part inside its tray

decision: A trigger is the button, so it draws one
why: the toolbar was not alone. Six trigger and close parts passed everything through, and all eight uses on the overlays page handed each one a whole button through render. A consumer writing the plain part got a browser default inside a styled popup
evidence: the kit had already answered this twice — the select trigger draws over the input, the toolbar button over the button — and Base UI's own examples style the trigger directly rather than wrapping one. Consistency with two precedents beat inventing a third shape
result: dialog, popover, menu and tooltip triggers default to soft; the two close parts default to ghost, and the popover's to small, which is what the page was passing by hand. The page lost eight render props and its Button import

decision: The page looks the same after it, which is the point
why: the change swapped which element carries the classes, and a trigger that shifted a pixel or a shade would be a regression hiding inside a tidy-up
evidence: measured in the running page: all seven triggers are buttons at one height and one ink, the popover close is ghost small, the dialog's two are ghost and solid, and each one opens and closes what it owns
result: the popup staying mounted after a close is the hidden pane, not the change — it carries data-closed and data-ending-style with no animations to run, which is what a frozen exit looks like

decision: Nothing else in the kit draws nothing, so that family was the whole of it
why: after the triggers I expected more parts in the same position and went looking for every function that sets no class at all
evidence: eight came back and none of them is a defect: six are the roots that hold state and draw no element, one is the tooltip provider, and the last is a menu group, which is a wrapper with a role and nothing to paint
result: the sweep is finished rather than paused. A new part that draws nothing would now stand out against eight that have a reason

decision: Two things I called clipped at phone width are drawn that way on purpose
why: I measured content wider than its own box and read the list as a defect list
evidence: the aurora's overflow is its two blur layers, which are meant to bleed past the card and be cut by it. The icon tile's label is a grid column at 0fr that opens on hover, so a nine pixel box is the closed state and not a squeezed one
result: the measurement was right and the reading was wrong. A box narrower than its content is only a defect when something was meant to be read

decision: The kit clears the 24px target minimum by four pixels, and only because of one gap
why: nine pages at 375px scroll sideways nowhere and clip nothing that matters, but three controls are under the minimum: the checkbox and radio at 18 square and the switch at 30 by 18
evidence: the exception carries them — a 24px circle on each centre touches nothing. Counted in the page: 28px between radio centres and 56px anywhere else. The label toggles its control, so the words are a second target, but they are a separate box and neither box is tall enough on its own
result: the radio group is the only adjacency the kit owns, so it is the only one it can promise. The rule reads the radio's own size class and each layout's gap and adds them; dropping the stacked gap to four pixels fails it at 22

decision: The icon tile has the tooltip's problem and the kit already shipped its answer
why: the tile opens its name on hover or on keyboard focus, and a phone offers neither, so a sighted reader there sees an icon and never learns what it is
evidence: emulated touch at 375px: hover: hover is false, the pointer is coarse, and a tap leaves the label nine pixels wide while the held-open tile beside it shows sixty-eight. The name is in the markup throughout, so a screen reader is told either way
result: the open variant is the answer and the page already demonstrates it, so this is a contract nobody had written down rather than a thing to build. It is now in the component's own docs and beside the tooltip paragraph, where the same story is already told

decision: A claim in the README rests on one variant branch, so that branch is pinned
why: the advice to reach for open is a claim about a variant, not about a component, and open: false is an empty object — the whole of the behaviour lives in the one branch that could be emptied by accident
evidence: the rule asks the two branches to differ and names the column each draws. Emptying the open branch fails it, which is exactly the edit that would leave the README telling a reader to do something that no longer works
